```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(cfbstats)
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(ggiraph)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)
# altdoc renders in a temp dir; point the knit wd at the project root so
# data/*.parquet and tar_read() resolve (CFBSTATS_ROOT is set in the site build).
root <- cfbstats_root()
if (nzchar(root)) {
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
}

set_girafe_defaults(
  opts_hover = opts_hover(
    css = "stroke:#111827;stroke-width:2.5px;filter:brightness(1.12);"
  ),
  opts_hover_inv = opts_hover_inv(css = "opacity:0.45;"),
  opts_tooltip = opts_tooltip(
    css = "background:#111827;color:#fff;padding:6px 9px;border-radius:5px;font-weight:bold;font-size:15px;"
  ),
  opts_zoom = opts_zoom(min = 1, max = 5),
  opts_toolbar = opts_toolbar(saveaspng = TRUE, position = "topright"),
  opts_sizing = opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: registry
#| include: false
# Standard: key on athlete id, never name (recruiting ids collide, decision 0013).
# The cfb_athlete_id here are the shared CFBD athlete namespace; each was resolved
# from the cleaned player_stats by name and QA-verified by its season/team pattern
# below — this post does not generalize the name lookup.
subjects <- tibble::tribble(
  ~who                 , ~cfb_athlete_id , ~gsis_id    ,
  "Arch Manning"       , "4870906"       , NA_character_,
  "Nicco Marchiol"     , "4685459"       , NA_character_,
  "Jordan Travis"      , "4360799"       , "00-0039797",
  "Cam Ward"           , "4688380"       , "00-0040676",
  "Trinidad Chambliss" , "4911529"       , NA_character_,
  "Joe Burrow"         , "3915511"       , "00-0036442",
  "Malachi Nelson"     , "4870928"       , NA_character_
)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
*Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-10-16. Careers of recent
classes (Manning, Marchiol, Chambliss, Nelson, Ward's Titans tenure) are
right-censored — later seasons may not yet be present.*
:::

I have expectations about these players. You probably do too. Seven
quarterbacks whose careers the college football internet narrates with
confidence: a redshirt-freshman-slash-double-medical-redshirt at two schools,
a guy who "redshirted then transferred" on the way to the #1 overall pick, a
five-year QB whose college injury ended everything, three multi-transfer
portal-era journeymen, and the most-hyped prospect in modern memory.

Here's the thing about expectations: they're testable claims. The whole point
of building this pipeline with data contracts is that a claim about the data
should either survive contact with the tables or leave an explicit bruise. So
this post is a ledger. I take each expectation, translate it into what the
database *could* show, and report what it actually shows — including the
places where the honest answer is "the data cannot see this," which is itself
a finding, and in a couple of places a bug report.

## The data spine

```{r}
#| label: build-spine
#| include: false
con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), "data/cfbstats.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)
ids_sql <- paste(sprintf("'%s'", subjects$cfb_athlete_id), collapse = ",")

# Roster backbone + eligibility flags (derived table, decision 0021).
flags <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT playerId, season, team, position, class_year, has_stats,
          redshirt_season, redshirt_career, fifth_year_career
   FROM roster_flags WHERE playerId IN (%s) ORDER BY playerId, season", ids_sql))
flags <- flags |>
  mutate(who = subjects$who[match(playerId, subjects$cfb_athlete_id)])

career <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT * FROM career_summary WHERE playerId IN (%s)", ids_sql)) |>
  mutate(who = subjects$who[match(playerId, subjects$cfb_athlete_id)])

college_picks <- dbGetQuery(con, sprintf(
  "SELECT CAST(collegeAthleteId AS VARCHAR) AS pid, year, round, pick, overall,
          name, nflTeam FROM picks WHERE CAST(collegeAthleteId AS VARCHAR) IN (%s)",
  ids_sql))
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

# Usage: passing attempts per season from the long stats table.
stats <- open_dataset("data/player_stats.parquet") |>
  filter(playerId %in% subjects$cfb_athlete_id) |>
  select(playerId, season, team, category, statType, stat) |>
  collect()
attempts <- stats |>
  filter(category == "passing", statType == "ATT") |>
  transmute(playerId, season, attempts = as.numeric(stat))

spine <- flags |>
  left_join(attempts, by = c("playerId", "season")) |>
  # CFBD id reuse is excluded from career populations (decision 0022); assert
  # none of these subjects were caught by that exclusion.
  left_join(career |> select(who, seasons, teams, transfers, gap_seasons), by = "who")

stopifnot(
  nrow(spine) > 0,
  all(subjects$who %in% spine$who),
  !anyNA(spine$has_stats),
  # A missing attempts value should occur only on a no-stat (redshirt-shaped)
  # season — assert that, so the figure's "RS" label is never a lie.
  all(is.na(spine$attempts) == !spine$has_stats)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: team-colors
#| include: false
teams <- open_dataset("data/teams.parquet") |>
  select(team, color) |>
  collect()
spine <- spine |>
  left_join(teams, by = c("team" = "team")) |>
  # FCS/D2 programs can sit outside teams.parquet; fall back to gray.
  mutate(color = if_else(is.na(color), "#9CA3AF", color),
         tooltip = paste0(who, " · ", team, " · ", season,
                          if_else(is.na(attempts), "", paste0(" · ", attempts, " pass att"))))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-timeline
#| fig-cap: "Season-by-season college timelines for the seven subjects, in team colors. The number is passing attempts that season; 'RS' marks a redshirt-SHAPED flag (a no-stat season followed by another observed season). The hole in Trinidad Chambliss's row is a missing 2024 — the database has no Ferris State roster row for the season he won a Division II national championship."
rel_lum <- function(hex) {
  m <- grDevices::col2rgb(hex) / 255
  lin <- ifelse(m <= 0.03928, m / 12.92, ((m + 0.055) / 1.055)^2.4)
  0.2126 * lin[1, ] + 0.7152 * lin[2, ] + 0.0722 * lin[3, ]
}
p <- ggplot(spine, aes(x = season, y = who)) +
  geom_tile_interactive(
    aes(fill = color, tooltip = tooltip, data_id = paste(who, season)),
    color = "white", height = 0.75
  ) +
  geom_text_interactive(
    aes(label = if_else(is.na(attempts), "RS", as.character(attempts)),
        data_id = paste(who, season)),
    color = if_else(rel_lum(spine$color) < 0.5, "white", "#111827"),
    size = 3.2, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2026) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_cfbstats(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "none")
girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 9.5, height_svg = 4)
```

Before the case files, one table the figure can't show — the per-career
summaries the pipeline derives from the roster backbone:

```{r}
#| label: career-table
career |>
  select(who, seasons, first_season, last_season, teams, transfers, gap_seasons) |>
  kable(caption = "Career summaries from the roster backbone (decision 0021).")
```

## Case files

### Arch Manning, Texas: "current player"

Expectation: on the Texas roster right now, waiting his turn, then starting.

```{r}
#| label: arch-table
spine |> filter(who == "Arch Manning") |>
  select(season, team, class_year, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Arch Manning, season by season.")
```

Confirmed, with texture. Four Texas seasons, 2023–2026, all still in the
data's present. But "waiting his turn" is not a binary in this data: he
recorded **5 pass attempts** in 2023 and **90** in 2024 before 404 in 2025.
The `has_stats` flag is TRUE for the backup years, so nothing about his
apprenticeship looks like a redshirt — it looks like a fifth-rounder's worth
of passing volume hiding inside a roster row. If you wanted "backup year" as
a feature, you'd need an attempts threshold, not a stat-presence flag. That
is a design choice this post now has opinions about.

### Nicco Marchiol, West Virginia → Northwestern: "he redshirted twice"

Expectation: a redshirt freshman year at WVU to preserve eligibility, then a
medical redshirt in a later WVU season, now at Northwestern.

```{r}
#| label: marchiol-table
spine |> filter(who == "Nicco Marchiol") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, redshirt_season) |>
  kable(caption = "Nicco Marchiol, season by season.")
```

**The data shows no redshirt at all.** Zero redshirt-shaped seasons, zero gap
seasons, five consecutive roster seasons with a stat line each. Now — I
believe the redshirts happened; the real-world record says so. But look at
what the data *can* see: 13 attempts in 2022, then 53, 56, and 98. A medical
redshirt after appearing in four games with 56 attempts leaves a stat line,
and a stat line is all `has_stats` and the redshirt flag know about. The
pipeline's redshirt flag is explicitly redshirt-*shaped*, not certified
(decision 0021), and this is the sharpest demonstration of that caveat I've
found yet: **two known redshirts, zero flags.** The flag catches quiet
seasons; it cannot catch quiet careers.

### Jordan Travis, Louisville → Florida State: "injured in his last year, drafted, never played an NFL snap"

Expectation: redshirts at Louisville, five years at FSU, the COVID year pads
him to five, a late-season injury in his final year, drafted anyway, never
takes another snap.

```{r}
#| label: travis-table
spine |> filter(who == "Jordan Travis") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Jordan Travis, season by season. Note two rows for 2021.")
```

Mostly confirmed, one correction, one artifact.

The correction: **he didn't redshirt at Louisville — he played.** 14 pass
attempts in 2018. The expectation as commonly told ("redshirted at
Louisville") is contradicted by the stat line; the truth is messier, a
mid-career transfer after a season he spent mostly holding a clipboard with a
few snaps attached. Meanwhile 2019 at FSU shows 11 attempts — his own injury
year — and then the climb: 131, 194, 353, 324.

The artifact is worse. Two rows for 2021: Florida State *and* Louisville.
Jordan Travis did not play at Louisville in 2021. This duplicate survives the
cleaning stage into `roster` and therefore into every downstream join — and
since `roster_flags` and `career_summary` build on it, his counts inherit it.
That's not a curiosity; that's a contract gap (no uniqueness guarantee on
`(playerId, season, team)`), and it should get one.

The NFL side is where the data is most satisfyingly unambiguous. He was
drafted — round 5, pick 171 overall, 2024, New York — and appears on exactly
one NFL roster season (NYJ, 2024), with **zero rows in the NFL player-stats
table**. The expectation "drafted, never played another snap" is not an
opinion here; it is literally the absence of rows, and the absence is the
finding. Right-censoring doesn't even complicate it: six seasons of
Burrow-style stat rows sit one id away, and Travis has none.

### Cam Ward, Incarnate Word → Washington State → Miami → Titans: "the multi-transfer"

Expectation: three schools, then the #1 pick.

```{r}
#| label: ward-table
spine |> filter(who == "Cam Ward") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Cam Ward, season by season.")

college_picks |> filter(pid == "4688380") |>
  select(year, round, pick, overall, nflTeam) |>
  kable(caption = "Cam Ward's draft slot (CFBD picks).")
```

The transfers check out exactly: three schools, two transfers, four roster
seasons, drafted first overall in 2025. But his FCS origin is where the data
goes soft. There is **no 2020 row at all** — the COVID-fallout FCS season,
which Incarnate Word played in spring 2021 — and the 2021 season shows only
**47 pass attempts** for a player who threw one of the most prolific FCS
passing seasons on record. CFBD's per-player stat coverage for lower
divisions is partial, and the pipeline's stat-line coverage contract was
written with FBS expectations. Two consequences: Ward's college totals in
this data undercount him, and — more importantly for the modeling goal —
FCS/D2 origins systematically generate thin or absent early seasons, so any
"career shape" feature will quietly misclassify players like Ward and
Chambliss as late starters rather than under-covered ones.

And the recruiting table, per its own untrusted-namespace design (decision
0013), **does not contain Cam Ward at all**. He was genuinely unranked out of
high school. "Unrated" is a real category, not an imputation target —
this case is exactly why decision 0013 says so.

### Trinidad Chambliss, Ferris State → Ole Miss: "D2 to the SEC"

```{r}
#| label: chambliss-table
spine |> filter(who == "Trinidad Chambliss") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, redshirt_season) |>
  kable(caption = "Trinidad Chambliss, season by season.")
```

Expectation: Ferris State (Division 2), then Ole Miss. The data agrees on the
shape and disagrees on the middle. 2023 at Ferris State carries a
redshirt-shaped flag — no stats, followed by observed seasons, the textbook
signature. Then **2024 is missing entirely**: no Ferris State roster row, no
stat line, nothing. The derived career summary dutifully records this as
`gap_seasons = 1`, which is precisely the wrong conclusion — that "gap" is
the season he started and won a Division II national championship. CFBD's
roster coverage simply doesn't reach Division 2 in 2024.

This is the cleanest possible demonstration of why `gap_seasons` needs an
accomplice before it becomes a feature: a gap flag computed over a
coverage-limited table measures *coverage* at least as much as it measures
careers. Chambliss is not an edge case — he's the quarterback of a top-ranked
SEC team right now.

### Joe Burrow, Ohio State → LSU: "redshirted at one school, then transferred to another"

```{r}
#| label: burrow-table
spine |> filter(who == "Joe Burrow") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts, redshirt_season) |>
  kable(caption = "Joe Burrow, season by season.")

college_picks |> filter(pid == "3915511") |>
  select(year, round, pick, overall, nflTeam) |>
  kable(caption = "Joe Burrow's draft slot (CFBD picks).")
```

Expectation: redshirt at Ohio State, grad-transfer to LSU, #1 pick. Here the
data *over*-delivers. Two seasons get redshirt-shaped flags — 2014 **and**
2015. But 2015 was not a redshirt; Burrow was an active backup who happened
to record zero of anything the feed carries (0 attempts in 2016's 28-attempt
season's neighbor years — 2016 shows 28 attempts, 2017 shows 11). A
stat-presence flag cannot distinguish "redshirted" from "dressed and never
thrown to." So the case confirms the mechanism and exposes its false-positive
rate: one real redshirt, two flags. Any feature built on `redshirt_season`
inherits a known, quantifiable over-count, which is exactly the kind of thing
you want to know *before* the model does.

His recruiting row is absent too — the class of 2015 sits inside the
recruiting table's 2010–2026 span, so this is a coverage or name-resolution
miss, not a range problem. The #1 pick in the data's own draft table has no
recruiting record. Worth an issue, not a shrug.

### Malachi Nelson, USC → Boise State → UTEP → Syracuse: "the other multi-transfer"

```{r}
#| label: nelson-table
spine |> filter(who == "Malachi Nelson") |>
  select(season, team, has_stats, attempts) |>
  kable(caption = "Malachi Nelson, season by season.")
```

Expectation: redshirt year at USC, then the portal carousel. The transfers
check out perfectly — four teams, three transfers, the largest transfer count
in this sample. The redshirt is invisible, for the most instructive reason in
this post: 2023 shows **3 pass attempts**. A flag built on stat presence
reads that season as played. Combine this with Marchiol (two real redshirts,
zero flags) and Burrow (zero-volume backup, two flags) and the pattern is
complete: **usage, not presence, is the observable; eligibility events are
not.** A redshirt proxy has to be an attempts-and-games threshold with an
explicit uncertainty band, or it will be quietly wrong in both directions.

## The bug the sample wasn't looking for

While verifying these careers, `class_year` fell over. In the cleaned roster,
`class_year` is supposed to be an eligibility class from 1–5. Here is its
actual distribution:

```{r}
#| label: class-year-audit
con2 <- dbConnect(duckdb(), "data/cfbstats.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)
cy <- dbGetQuery(con2, "SELECT class_year, COUNT(*) AS n FROM roster_flags
                        GROUP BY class_year ORDER BY n DESC")
dbDisconnect(con2, shutdown = TRUE)
cy |> head(10) |> kable(caption = "class_year distribution (top 10 of 24 distinct values).")
```

Twenty-four distinct values, including what appear to be whole *seasons*
(2010–2026) inside an eligibility column. Every `fifth_year_career` flag and
any class-based feature inherits this contamination. The redshirt-shaped
flags don't depend on `class_year` (they're built on stat gaps), but the
fifth-year flag does, and the range contract for `class_year` apparently
isn't enforcing 1–5 where it matters. This one goes in the ledger as a bug,
not a caveat.

## The ledger

| Expectation | Data verdict |
|---|---|
| Arch Manning is at Texas now | Confirmed — 4 seasons, with a 5 → 90 → 404-attempt apprenticeship |
| Marchiol redshirted twice | **Invisible** — stat lines every season; redshirt-shaped flags catch quiet seasons, not quiet usage |
| Travis redshirted at Louisville | **Contradicted** — he recorded 14 attempts there in 2018 |
| Travis: 5 FSU years, injured, drafted, no NFL snaps | Confirmed — draft slot present, one NFL roster season, zero NFL stat rows |
| Ward: 3 transfers to the #1 pick | Confirmed — but his FCS years are under-covered (no 2020, 47 attempts in 2021), and he's absent from recruiting entirely |
| Chambliss: Ferris State → Ole Miss | Confirmed with a hole — the 2024 D2 championship season is a missing row masquerading as a "gap" |
| Burrow: redshirt then transfer to #1 pick | Confirmed and **over-flagged** — two redshirt-shaped seasons for one real redshirt |
| Nelson: USC redshirt then 3 transfers | Transfers confirmed (4 teams); the redshirt is 3 attempts of invisible |

Three things I'd carry out of this post into the pipeline:

1. **Redshirt flags need a usage-based definition** (attempts/games
   thresholds), not stat presence — Marchiol, Nelson, and Burrow between them
   show every failure mode.
2. **`(playerId, season, team)` uniqueness in `roster` needs a contract** —
   the Travis 2021 duplicate is real and downstream.
3. **`class_year` is contaminated with season values** and the fifth-year
   flag built on it is untrustworthy until cleaned and contracted.

The database passed most of my expectations, which is almost the least
interesting result. The interesting results are the three ways it is
*structurally* blind — quiet usage, lower-division coverage, and a quietly
broken eligibility column — because those are the shapes that will bias
exactly the model this project exists to build.

<SUGGESTION>Add the (playerId, season, team) uniqueness contract and the class_year range contract to R/contracts.R.</SUGGESTION>
